neighbours.label: the token ' hash' in cryptographic contexts (hash function, a hash of the data)
fire: Each block stores the hash of the previous block in the chain.
The server compares the password hash against the stored value.
A secure hash function makes collisions very hard to find.
Git identifies every commit by a hash of its contents.
The download page lists a SHA-256 hash for each release file.
Changing one bit of the input changes the whole hash output.
The signature is computed over a hash of the message body.
Store only a salted hash, never the plain password itself.
quiet: Each block stores the timestamp of the previous block in the chain.
The server compares the password entered against the stored value.
A secure cipher makes the message very hard to read without the key.
Git identifies every commit by its author and a short message.
The download page lists the file size for each release file.
Changing one bit of the input changes the whole encrypted output.
The signature is computed over the full message body.
Store only an encrypted copy, never the plain password itself.
